description: Block a write that introduces an em dash or an AI-tic sentence fragment into markdown. Enforces the markdown instructions instead of only stating them (Claude Code PostToolUse).

hooks.command: jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // .tool_response.filePath // empty' | while IFS= read -r f; do case "$f" in *.md|*.mdx|*.qmd) if [ -f "$f" ] && grep -qF "$(printf '\xe2\x80\x94')" "$f"; then n=$(grep -nF "$(printf '\xe2\x80\x94')" "$f" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); jq -n --arg f "$f" --arg n "$n" '{decision:"block", reason: ("Em dash found in " + $f + " at line " + $n + ". Replace it with a comma, period, colon, or parentheses, per the markdown instructions. Fix it before continuing.")}'; fi ;; esac; done

hooks.prompt: You are a markdown style linter enforcing this repo's prose rules (.github/instructions/markdown.instructions.md) on NEWLY WRITTEN text only. Ignore anything already in the file before this edit, code blocks, and short table or list label cells. Hook input (Write or Edit tool call): $ARGUMENTS. Only check .md/.mdx/.qmd files; for any other file respond with exactly {"decision":"allow"}. For markdown files, check the new prose (tool_input.content for Write, tool_input.new_string for Edit) against these rules: (1) full sentences, not fragments glued together with commas where a period belongs; (2) no 'not X, but Y' or 'not just X' contrastive tic used as a stylistic habit; (3) no colon-into-noun-phrase-fragment construction such as 'X: a direction, not a task, something that...'. If any rule is broken, respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else: {"decision":"block","reason":"<quote the offending sentence, name the rule it breaks, one sentence>"}. If the new prose is clean, respond with exactly {"decision":"allow"}. Output ONLY the JSON object, no other text.
